thread:
incident-bot: :warning: Pager: sustained elevated 5xx and timeouts for /v1/chat.stream in eu-central-1. Error rate rising from 3% -> 28% over 8m. Pager: P1. Oncall: Ravi K.
Ravi K.: I'm on it, joining now. Any customer reports?
Support Eng: two customers opened high-priority tickets showing timeout traces and 502/503s. They attached request IDs that consistently fail.
Elena M.: looking at gateway logs — lots of upstream 502s coming back from runtime pods, many with exit code 139. Correlates with a spike in concurrent batches at ~21:42 UTC.
Ravi K.: exit 139 is segfault. OpsBot, any infra alerts?
OpsBot: Host-level alert: kernel OOM events on nodes infer-eu-02* and infer-eu-05*. dmesg excerpts attached.
Elena M.: past logs show repeated mmap allocation failures in allocator: `mmap(NULL, 0x3b9aca00, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0) = -1 ENOMEM (Cannot allocate memory)` then followed by `Segmentation fault (core dumped)` inside libflash_attention.so.
Support Eng: the failing request patterns are batched multi-turn chats with long history + function-calls; payload sizes up to 45MB per request.
Ravi K.: root hypothesis: allocator/memory fragmentation under bursty batching causes mmap failures and then attention kernel deref leads to segfault. We need immediate mitigation to reduce tail memory pressure.
Elena M.: mitigation plan (live): 1) reduce per-request max_batch_size from 8 -> 4, 2) apply per-route concurrency cap for offending tenants, 3) enable per-pod memory overcommit guard to proactively reject requests that would exceed soft allocation limits. Rolling changes now.
runtime-team: deploying config roll to cap batch_size and enable ALLOC_SOFT_LIMIT=0.85. Also toggling ATTENTION_FALLBACK=1 to use CPU-safe fallback for affected kernels.
pagerduty-bot: Pager acknowledged by Ravi K. (oncall).
Ravi K.: also start draining nodes with repeated OOMs. Elena, coordinate node replacement with infra.
Elena M.: draining infer-eu-05 and infer-eu-02; launching node replacements with updated driver/kernel (hotfix: nmalloc fragmentation patch) and runtime patched to check mmap return before deref.
Support Eng: notifying customers that we throttled heavy requests and applied temporary caps; they're asking if we'll replay missing requests — we can't, will provide logs for troubleshooting.
runtime-team: quick hotfix pushed: check for NULL from mmap and fail gracefully with 429/524 instead of crashing. Rolling across 40% of pods.
Ravi K.: good. Any sign the canary is reducing 5xx? Elena?
Elena M.: yes, after 6 minutes the error rate in the canary pool dropped from 28% -> 6%. Global rate now 9% and trending down. Nodes still showing occasional OOM traces but new nodes healthy.
Customer Success: sending structured update to affected customers: timeline, mitigation steps, ETA for full resolution. They're requesting timeframe for permanent fix.
Ravi K.: assign owners for follow-ups: 1) runtime-team -> patch allocator and add stress test for fragmentation (owner: runtime-team), 2) infra -> kernel/driver upgrade rollout (owner: Elena), 3) product -> tenant long-history quota and per-tenant burst protections (owner: Product Ops).
runtime-team: opening PR #4987 with allocator fix and adding fuzz test that simulates fragmented heaps under heavy batching. Will backport to stable.
Elena M.: replacing 4 nodes now; expected done in 10m.
OpsBot: runbook triggered: "Runtime segfaults/oom during inference". Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/segfault-oom. Steps executed: cap batch, enable fallback, drain & replace nodes, notify customers.
runtime-team: adding telemetry: track mmap failures, attention-fallback counts, and per-tenant request sizes.
Ravi K.: brief customer impact summary for post-incident: Impact window ~21:41:12 -> 22:05:34 UTC. A subset of eu-central-1 customers experienced increased 5xx/timeouts; no data corruption; affected requests either failed with 5xx or were rejected during mitigation.
Support Eng: customers acknowledged and requested postmortem + mitigations.
Ravi K.: we'll run full RCA doc and include timeline + mitigations. Priorities: permanent allocator fix, improved canarying for batch-size changes, and tenant-level long-history safeguards.
Customer Success: confirming customers content for now; asking for estimated ETA for code fix — runtime-team estimates 3 business days for CR + 1 week for rollout.
Ravi K.: thanks everyone, marking incident mitigated in pager after sustained drop to baseline. Leaving this thread for postmortem details and assigning owners. Closing live coordination.
